  "summary": "Adversarial review of the three specialist critiques (R1_graphs, R2_numerics, R3_inference) against the executed code and audit tables confirms the primary technical results while rejecting several specialist overclaims. First, all 336 prior graphs reconstruct with exact SHA-256 mask agreement and identical node-by-node degree sequences in triangle arms (Arms 1 and 2), and all 144 baseline mechanical reference rows (128 unique cases) reproduce with zero discrepancy. Second, all 384 L=24 mechanical control solves converged (max force residual 3.72e-10, max uncapped rate argument 1.046 < 30 with zero rate-cap activations at sampled update steps), and all 96 eligible fine-step comparisons (rate_beta=10) pass the predeclared per-case gate |retention(0.05) - retention(0.025)| <= 1e-4 (max 9.61e-5). However, key specialist claims require correction: (1) R2's analytic ~0.0034 bound on rate sensitivity (from 0.5*exp(-5)) is invalid for bending-coupled networks (kappa > 0), and existing dt=0.1 transient traces show rate_beta=10 vs 0 shifts normalized stress by up to -0.0554 at t=0.5 despite similar t=5 retention; (2) R1's claim that degree-preserving 6-ring flips eliminate component-size confounding is falsified by L=24, z=2.4 giant-node variations, and R3's claim that fixing giant_nodes holds giant_mean_degree equal to z_actual fails whenever edges exist outside the giant component (200/336 graphs); (3) finite-graph degree histograms (which retain 15.6%-23.2% intermediate k=1..5 nodes at L=24 in Arm 3) refute a pure {0,6} distribution without testing chain stationarity or thermodynamic phases; (4) the 9/336 graphs with both directional wrap flags but winding rank 1 diagnose a coordinate-projection interpretation limit (diagonal (1,-1) cycles), not an implementation bug or a proven 'triangulated ribbon' geometry, while G0 <= 1e-6 exclusions in z=3.2, kappa=0 uniform graphs represent mechanical conditioning ineligibility rather than solver failure or a proven universal z_c=4.0 phase transition; and (5) deterministic graph reconstruction and same-model specialist agreement add audit observables and internal consistency checks, not independent statistical replication or external validation.",

      "evidence": "R2_numerics (line 80) claims baseline stretching relaxation exp(-5)=0.00674 structurally bounds beta=10 vs beta=0 differences to ~0.0034, and R1 (line 189), R2 (line 125), and R3 (line 41) claim beta=0 persistence uniquely demonstrates static stretching-bending energy partitioning. However, in analysis/TRANSIENT_RATE_AGGREGATES.json (lines 219-223), at L=24, z=4.8, kappa=0.003, t=0.5 (dt=0.1), beta=10 minus beta=0 shifts normalized stress by -0.04731 (uniform) and -0.05543 (hub), changing the hub-minus-uniform contrast from -0.00833 to -0.01645.",
      "implication": "In source/model.py (lines 81, 92-99), H = B.T@B + kap*(D.T@D) couples axial extensions e to memory q at every quasistatic step, slowing relaxation eigenmodes below the homogeneous unit rate when kappa > 0. Thus, 0.5*exp(-5) is not a valid bound on coupled stress tails. Moreover, beta=0 was only executed at dt=0.1 (source/controls.py line 11) without fine-step gating, and separate axial versus bending energy/stress terms were never logged. Persistence of the t=5 contrast at beta=0 (and zero cap activations with max argument 1.046 < 30 in analysis/RUN_SUMMARY.json lines 7-9) refutes a rate-acceleration-only or cap-clipping explanation at final time, but does not establish trajectory-wide rate invariance or isolate a unique energy-partition mechanism.",
      "recommended_check": "Reject the 0.0034 analytical bound for kappa > 0, qualify all beta=0 comparisons as unrefined dt=0.1 evaluations, and explicitly decompose axial ((e-(1-r)*q) stretching) versus bending (kap*D@u) stress/energy contributions before claiming a specific partitioning mechanism.",
      "claim_status": "simulation_result"
    },

      "evidence": "R1_graphs (line 179) states that Arm 1 vs Arm 2 degree-preserving rewiring eliminates component-size confounding, and claims (line 169) that intermediate k=1..5 degrees falsify a stationary thermodynamic phase. Mechanically, G0 <= 1e-6 at z=3.2, kappa=0 is a predeclared conditioning/eligibility exclusion (rendering the paired contrast undefined, not zero) rather than a CG solver failure, and finite-graph single-mode G0 eligibility does not establish a thermodynamic central-force rigidity phase transition at z=4.0 (claimed by R2, line 90).",
      "recommended_check": "State explicitly that z=3.2, kappa=0 paired retention contrasts are undefined due to uniform-arm G0 conditioning ineligibility (not solver failure), avoid geometric 'ribbon' or universal z_c=4.0 phase-transition claims, and stratify descriptive L=24, z=3.2 hub metrics by giant_winding_rank (1 vs 2).",

      "title": "Unsupported RNG permutation-nesting claim in R3 versus intentional paired-seed blocking and non-independent model review",

      "evidence": "R3_inference (line 51) asserts that calling rng.choice(np.arange(d, 3*N, 3), min(N, round(z*N/6)), replace=False) in source/model.py (line 17) with seed integers 74000..74003 across z=3.2, 4.0, and 4.8 draws from an identical per-direction random permutation stream across coordination levels. Meanwhile, PROTOCOL.md (lines 9, 11) and analysis/RUN_SUMMARY.json (line 12) specify that the 4 seeds are descriptive paired blocks and that all four review calls use the same model family.",

  "strongest_surviving_claim": "All 336 prior graph treatment variants reconstruct with exact SHA-256 mask agreement and verified degree-sequence invariants, and across the four descriptive paired L=24 seed blocks at z in {3.2, 4.0, 4.8} and finite bending kappa in {0.003, 0.03}, the negative hub-minus-uniform t=5 stress-retention contrast (-42.62 to -1.94 percentage points at dt=0.025) passes the predeclared per-case time-step refinement gate (max |retention(0.05) - retention(0.025)| = 9.61e-5 <= 1e-4), experiences zero exponential rate-cap activations at sampled update states (max uncapped argument 1.046 < 30), and persists under constant-rate relaxation (rate_beta=0 at dt=0.1), ruling out time-step discretization drift, rate-cap clipping, and final-time strain-rate acceleration as explanations for the composite Arm 3 versus Arm 0 mechanical difference in this toy network model.",
  "decisive_next_experiment": "Ranked bounded CPU follow-up within the existing 4-seed L=24 framework: (1) Zero-new-simulation stress/energy audit: re-evaluate the saved displacement trajectories or run a lightweight diagnostic pass on existing L=24 cases to explicitly decompose total shear stress and elastic energy into axial stretching ((e - (1-r)*q) terms) versus collinear bending (kap * D @ u terms) over t in [0, 5], directly testing whether static stretching-to-bending mode partitioning explains both the t=5 beta=0 contrast and the t=0.5 transient rate sensitivity. (2) Bounded beta=0 time-step refinement: run dt=0.05 and dt=0.025 controls for rate_beta=0 on Arms 0 and 3 at L=24, z in {3.2, 4.0, 4.8}, kappa in {0.003, 0.03} (48 cases) to subject the constant-rate baseline and transient rate deltas to the exact same <= 1e-4 refinement gate as rate_beta=10. (3) Mechanism-isolation topology control: compare existing Arm 3 graphs against unmodified Arm 0 uniform graphs generated at z_target = 5.0 and 5.55 (matching the audited exact giant_mean_degree of Arm 3 at z=3.2 and 4.8) to bound how much of the retention drop is explained simply by giant-component coordination densification before attempting Metropolis-corrected constrained-rewiring ensembles.",
